Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/o/oladivi01.html|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=November 30, 2018}} is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Wisconsin Herd]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana Hoosiers]], where in the [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13 season]] he was named the [[Sporting News Men's College Basketball Player of the Year|''Sporting News'' Men's College Basketball Player of the Year]], the Co-[[NABC Defensive Player of the Year]], and a first-team [[2013 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] by the [[United States Basketball Writers Association|USBWA]] and ''[[Sporting News]]''. That year, he was also named the winner of the [[Adolph Rupp Trophy]], given annually to the top player in men's [[NCAA Division I]] [[basketball]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.ruppawards.com/previous.html |title=Adolph F. Rupp Trophies – Previous Winners |access-date=February 16, 2014 |archive-date=August 5, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210805040410/http://www.ruppawards.com/previous.html |url-status=dead }} Oladipo was drafted with the second overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Orlando Magic]] and went on to be named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie First Team]]. He was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in 2016 and then traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in 2017. He became a first-time [[NBA All-Star]], led the league in steals, was named to the All-Defensive First Team and the All-NBA Third Team, and won the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award]] in his first season with Indiana. Despite an injury-riddled 2018–19 season, including a season-ending injury in January 2019, Oladipo was named an Eastern Conference All-Star reserve for the second straight year. In January 2021, he was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]], but was dealt to the [[Miami Heat]] just two months later. He underwent season-ending surgery after just four games with Miami and made his playing return in March 2022. Oladipo is also a singer, having released an EP, ''Songs for You,'' in 2017, his debut full-length album ''V.O.'' in 2018,{{cite web |url=https://www.complex.com/sports/2018/11/victor-oladipo-debut-album-tells-us-what-nba-rappers-he-wants-to-collab-with|title=Pacers Star Victor Oladipo Breaks Down Debut Album, Tells Us What NBA Rappers He Wants to Collab with|website=[[Complex Networks]] }} and an [[afrobeats]]-inspired EP, ''TUNDE,'' in 2023.{{cite magazine |url=https://www.si.com/nba/heat/miami-news/miami-heats-victor-oladipo-released-his-new-afrobeats-album-tunde |title=Miami Heat's Victor Oladipo Released His New Afrobeats Album "TUNDE" [[File:20120105 Tim Hardaway Jr vs Victor Oladipo.jpg|thumb|left|Oladipo (left) guards [[Tim Hardaway Jr.]] of the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]] in 2012]] Oladipo chose to play basketball at [[Indiana University]], turning down offers from [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]], [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]], [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]] and others.{{cite web|title=Victor Oladipo|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/basketballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Victor-Oladipo-84192|work=Yahoo.com|access-date=April 7, 2012}} Upon his commitment to the [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Hoosiers]], he said, "It's like a basketball atmosphere everywhere you go....[[Bloomington, Indiana]] is a basketball town. That's perfect."{{cite news|last=Bozich|first=Alex|title=Victor Oladipo joins Indiana's 2010 class|url=http://www.insidethehall.com/2009/09/07/victor-oladipo-joins-indianas-2010-class/|access-date=April 7, 2012|work=insidethehall.com|date=September 7, 2009}} He joined during the [[2010–11 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|2010–11 season]], playing 32 games with five starts as a freshman, averaging 7.4 points, 3.7 rebounds and 1.1 steals in 18.0 minutes per game.{{cite web |title=Victor Oladipo College Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/victor-oladipo-1.html |website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com |access-date=4 February 2026 |language=en}} As a sophomore during the [[2011–12 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|2011–12 season]], Justin Albers from ''Inside the Hall'' referred him as "Indiana's most improved player this season".{{cite news|last=Albers|first=Justin|title=That's A Wrap: Victor Oladipo|url=http://www.insidethehall.com/2012/04/05/thats-a-wrap-victor-oladipo-2/|access-date=April 7, 2012|work=insidethehall.com|date=April 5, 2012}} In the [[2012 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2012 NCAA tournament]], the Hoosiers lost in the Sweet Sixteen to [[2011–12 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]].{{cite news |last1=Tipton |first1=Jerry |title=Kentucky gets revenge, dispatches Indiana 102-90 |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/ncaa/article44163453.html |access-date=February 3, 2026 |work=Lexington Herald Ledger |orig-date=March 23, 2012 |date=November 10, 2015}} In 36 games, he made 34 starts and averaged 10.8 points, 3.6 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.4 steals in 26.7 minutes per game. In the 2012–13 season, despite an Indiana roster deep with talent, Oladipo emerged as one of the nation's biggest stars.{{cite news | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/71398/oladipo-emerges-as-hoosiers-star | title=Oladipo emerges as Hoosiers' star | date=December 31, 2012 | access-date=January 1, 2013 | last=Brennan | first=Eamonn | publisher=ESPN}} Midway through the season, [[ESPN]] reporter Eamonn Brenann wrote, "In 2½ seasons in Bloomington, Oladipo has morphed from a raw athletic specimen to a defensive specialist/energy glue guy – he became a hit with IU fans for holding his hand in front of his face after dunks at home, typically after a steal he himself created – into a sudden, stunning, bona fide collegiate star." Due in part to Oladipo's leadership, the Indiana Hoosiers finished the 2012–13 season as the outright Big Ten champions.{{cite web |author1=Julie Rawe |title=IU Men's Basketball Team Wins Big-Ten Championship |url=https://indianapublicmedia.org/news/iu-mens-basketball-team-wins-bigten-championship-46359.php |website=Indiana Public Media |access-date=June 30, 2022 |language=English |date=March 11, 2013 |archive-date=September 26, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220926091836/https://indianapublicmedia.org/news/iu-mens-basketball-team-wins-bigten-championship-46359.php |url-status=dead }} At the end of the regular season, Oladipo ranked fourth in the country in field goal percentage (61.4), on pace to have the highest field goal percentage by any guard since the 1996–97 season.{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/79138/why-oladipo-should-win-wooden-award | title=Why Oladipo should win Wooden Award | publisher=ESPN | date=March 13, 2013 | access-date=March 13, 2013 | last=Feldman | first=Ryan}} Among Wooden Award finalists, he had the best net rating, which is the difference between points produced and points allowed per 100 possessions. Oladipo produced 42 more points than he allowed per 100 possessions. In 2012–13, Oladipo played and started in all 36 games, averaging 13.6 points, 6.3 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 2.2 steals in 28.4 minutes per game. He was subsequently named the [[Sporting News Men's College Basketball Player of the Year|''Sporting News'' Men's College Basketball Player of the Year]], the [[NABC Defensive Player of the Year|National Co-Defensive Player of the Year]], and a first-team [[2013 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] by the [[United States Basketball Writers Association|USBWA]] and ''[[Sporting News]]''. In conference honors, he was named a unanimous pick to the first-team All-Big Ten by both the coaches and media, and was named Big Ten Defensive Player of the year. ==Professional career== ===Orlando Magic (2013–2016)=== [[File:Victor Oladipo Magic.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Oladipo with the Magic in 2013]] On April 9, 2013, at a press conference with Tom Crean, Oladipo announced his decision to forgo his senior season at Indiana and enter the [[2013 NBA draft]]. He was projected as a top-15 pick by ESPN and CBS Sports. Oladipo was invited to sit in the "green room" during the draft and was selected second overall by the [[Orlando Magic]], later signing his [[Rookie scale contract|rookie-scale]] contract with the Magic on July 8.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/magic-sign-victor-oladipo|title=Magic sign Victor Oladipo|website=Orlando Magic|access-date=May 2, 2019}} When the 2013 rookie class convened for its annual photo shoot and filled out its NBA.com Rookie Survey, the class voted Oladipo as the best defender, the co-favorite 2013–14 Rookie of the Year (with [[CJ McCollum]]), the co-favorite to have the best career (with [[Kelly Olynyk]]) and second-most athletic (behind [[Tony Mitchell (basketball, born 1992)|Tony Mitchell]]).{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/features/john_schuhmann/08/26/2013-14-nba-rookie-survey/index.html|title=Magic's Oladipo among rookie favorites to stand out in 2013-14|access-date=October 15, 2013|date=August 26, 2013|author=Schuhmann, John|work=[[NBA.com]]}} On December 3, 2013, Oladipo recorded his first career triple-double with 26 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists in a double overtime loss to the Philadelphia 76ers. Rookie [[Michael Carter-Williams]] of the 76ers also recorded his first career triple-double in the same game, marking the first and only time in NBA history that two rookies have recorded triple-doubles in the same game.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20131203/ORLPHI/gameinfo.html|title=Magic at 76ers|website=NBA.com|access-date=May 2, 2019}} The last time that two players had recorded their first career triple-doubles in the same game was when Detroit Pistons' pair [[Donnie Butcher]] and [[Ray Scott (basketball)|Ray Scott]] did it on March 14, 1964 (they were not rookies). It was also the first time that two opponents had recorded triple-doubles in the same game since [[Caron Butler]] and [[Baron Davis]] had done so on November 23, 2007.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400489134|title=Michael Carter-Williams, 76ers overcome Arron Afflalo's 43 |date=December 3, 2013 |work=[[ESPN]] |access-date=December 4, 2013}} During the month of February, Oladipo participated in the [[Rising Stars Challenge]] and the [[NBA All-Star Weekend Skills Challenge|Taco Bell Skills Challenge]].{{cite web |author1=Josh Robbins |title=Magic's Victor Oladipo scores 22 points in Rising Stars Challenge |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/orlando-magic/os-oladipo-payton-rising-stars-challenge-0214-20150213-story.html |website=Orlando Sentinel |access-date=June 30, 2022 |language=English |date=February 14, 2014}}{{cite web |author1=Philip Rossman-Reich |title=Victor Oladipo, MCW fall in Taco Bell Skills Challenge Finals |url=https://orlandomagicdaily.com/2014/02/16/all-star-saturday-night-021514/ |website=Fansided |date=February 16, 2014 |access-date=June 30, 2022 |language=English |archive-date=April 15, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230415201105/https://orlandomagicdaily.com/2014/02/16/all-star-saturday-night-021514/ |url-status=dead }} Oladipo went on to finish second in the Rookie of the Year voting behind Carter-Williams.{{cite web |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/orlando-magic/os-mbb-victor-oladipo-second-in-rookie-of-year-20140505-post.html|title=Victor Oladipo finishes second in 2013-14 NBA Rookie of the Year Award voting |first=Josh |last=Robbins |date=May 5, 2014 |website=OrlandoSentinel.com |access-date=May 2, 2019}} [[File:Victor Oladipo Magic 2014.jpg|left|thumb|Oladipo with the Magic in 2014]] On October 24, 2014, Oladipo was ruled out indefinitely after suffering a facial fracture in practice the previous day.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/oladipo-out-indefinitely-facial-fracture|title=Oladipo Out Indefinitely With Facial Fracture|website=Orlando Magic|access-date=May 2, 2019}} Two days later, the Magic exercised their third-year team option on Oladipo's rookie scale contract, extending the contract through the 2015–16 season.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/magic-exercise-contract-options-fournier-harkless-nicholson-and-oladipo|title=Magic Exercise Contract Options on Fournier, Harkless, Nicholson and Oladipo|website=Orlando Magic|access-date=May 2, 2019}} He made his return from injury on November 14 wearing a facial protection mask as he made his season debut against the Milwaukee Bucks. In 25 minutes off the bench, he recorded 13 points, 3 rebounds and 2 assists in a 101–85 win.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141114/MILORL/gameinfo.html|title=Bucks at Magic|website=NBA.com|access-date=May 2, 2019}} During the [[2015 NBA All-Star Game|2015 NBA All-Star Weekend]], Oladipo competed in the Rising Stars Challenge and the Slam Dunk Contest,{{cite news|url=https://www.wthr.com/article/zeller-oladipo-named-to-nbas-rising-stars-all-star-roster|title=Zeller, Oladipo named to NBA's Rising Stars all-star roster|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 28, 2015|website=13 WTHR Indianapolis|access-date=May 2, 2019|archive-date=July 5, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180705003706/https://www.wthr.com/article/zeller-oladipo-named-to-nbas-rising-stars-all-star-roster|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2015/02/14/victor-oladipo-completes-540-degree-slam-in-first-round-of-dunk-contest-video/|title=Victor Oladipo completes 540-degree slam in first round of dunk contest (VIDEO)|first=Brett|last=Pollakoff|date=February 15, 2015|website=nbcsports.com|access-date=May 2, 2019}} finishing second in the dunk contest behind [[Zach LaVine]]. On March 4, 2015, Oladipo scored a career-high 38 points on 15-of-25 shooting in a loss to the Phoenix Suns.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150304/PHXORL/gameinfo.html|title=Suns at Magic|website=NBA.com|access-date=May 2, 2019}} On October 25, 2015, the Magic exercised their fourth-year team option on Oladipo's rookie scale contract, extending the contract through the 2016–17 season.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-exercise-team-options-gordon-napier-oladipo-and-payton|title=Magic Exercise Team Options on Gordon, Napier, Oladipo and Payton|website=Orlando Magic|access-date=May 2, 2019}} Five days later, he recorded his second career triple-double with 21 points, 13 rebounds and 10 assists in a double-overtime loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder. He also hit a buzzer-beating three-pointer to send the game into double overtime.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151030/OKCORL/gameinfo.html|title=Thunder vs Magic|website=NBA.com|access-date=May 2, 2019}} Oladipo averaged just 12.8 points per game over his first 12 games of the season. Head coach [[Scott Skiles]] moved Oladipo to a bench role for the Magic's November 25 game against the New York Knicks.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151125/NYKORL/gameinfo.html|title=Knicks vs Magic|website=NBA.com|access-date=May 2, 2019}} Oladipo continued coming off the bench following this performance, averaging 17.0 points, 5.4 rebounds, 4.5 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.4 blocks over his first eight games off the bench.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/o/oladivi01/gamelog/2016/|title=Victor Oladipo 2015-16 Game Log|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=May 2, 2019}} On January 4, he started for the Magic for the first time since November 23. In 34 minutes of action, he recorded a team-high 18 points, 7 rebounds, 5 assists and 2 steals in a loss to the Detroit Pistons.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160104/ORLDET/gameinfo.html|title=Magic vs Pistons|website=NBA.com|access-date=May 2, 2019}} On March 18, he scored a career-high 45 points in a 109–103 loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers, becoming the ninth player in franchise history to score 40 points in a game and the first Magic player to do so since [[Arron Afflalo]] in December 2013.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160318/CLEORL/gameinfo.html|title=Cavaliers vs Magic|website=NBA.com|access-date=May 2, 2019}} Oladipo missed the final three games of the season with a concussion.{{cite web|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/orlando-magic/os-orlando-magic-news-0413-20160412-story.html|title=Victor Oladipo is feeling better after 2nd concussion of the season|first=Josh|last=Robbins|website=OrlandoSentinel.com|date=April 12, 2016 |access-date=May 2, 2019}} ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2016–2017)=== [[File:Victor Oladipo 2017.jpg|thumb|upright|Oladipo with the Thunder in 2017]] On June 23, 2016, Oladipo was traded, along with [[Ersan İlyasova]] and the draft rights to [[Domantas Sabonis]], to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in exchange for [[Serge Ibaka]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/acquisitions_160623|title=Thunder Acquires Oladipo, Ilyasova and Draft Rights to Sabonis|website=Oklahoma City Thunder|access-date=May 2, 2019}} He made his debut for the Thunder in their season opener on October 26, scoring 10 points in 26 minutes as a starter in a 103–97 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899389|title=Thunder vs. 76ers – Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=October 26, 2016|access-date=October 27, 2016}} On October 31, he signed a four-year, $84 million contract extension with the Thunder.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/extensions-161031|title=Thunder Signs Adams, Oladipo to Multi-Year Contract Extensions|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=October 31, 2016|access-date=October 31, 2016}}{{cite web|last=Charania|first=Shams|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/sources-oladipo-thunder-agree-to-84m-extension-200751727.html|title=Sources: Victor Oladipo, Thunder agree to $84M extension|work=Yahoo.com|date=October 31, 2016|access-date=October 31, 2016}} A right wrist injury in mid-December forced Oladipo to miss nine straight games.{{cite 2016}} He returned to action on December 31 and scored 15 points against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899949|title=Westbrook leads Thunder past Coming off the bench for the Pacers, he scored 9 points in 21 minutes of playing time, including a game-tying three-pointer, in an overtime win over the Chicago Bulls.{{cite web|title=Box Crean (basketball)|Tom Crean]] would frequently attribute Oladipo's success to his extreme work ethic and pre-game preparation of reviewing film. Oladipo is known for entertaining fans with exciting dunks. As announcer [[Clark Kellogg]] noted, "Victor Oladipo is like a baby's bottom, smooth and sometimes... explosive."{{cite web | url=http://network.yardbarker.com/college_basketball/article_external/clark_kellogg_compares_victor_oladipo_to_a/12885628/ | title=Announcer's odd comparison for Oladipo | publisher=Yard Barker | access-date=February 10, 2013}} On offense, Oladipo is capable of aggressively and quickly [[Penetration (basketball)|driving]] to the basket, aided by his leaping ability. Following a victory by Indiana over #1 ranked Michigan, coach [[John Beilein]] remarked, "I've seen a lot of players. I don't know whether I've seen one quicker or faster, more athletic, than Oladipo. It's tough to stay in front of him."{{cite web | url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/ncaab--indiana-beats-michigan--no--1-ranking-awaits-college-basketball-s-most-entertaining-team-070029295.html | title=Indiana beats Michigan; No. 1 ranking awaits college basketball's most entertaining team | publisher=Yahoo! | access-date=February 3, 2013 | author=Forde, Pat| date=February 3, 2013 }} His offensive proficiency improved as his outside shooting range improved each year of his collegiate career. On defense, Oladipo has been described as a "lockdown off-ball defender who can defend multiple positions".{{cite web | url=https://insider.espn.com/blog/ncbexperts/ | title=Top 10 closers in college hoops | work=ESPN.com | date=February 5, 2013 | access-date=February 5, 2013 | author=Greenberg, Seth}} He has the quickness to guard point guards and the strength and athleticism to guard a forward if caught in a mismatch. His athleticism and anticipation makes it hard to set a screen on him. He also rebounds well at his position. ==Television appearance== In 2019, Oladipo competed in [[The Masked Singer (American TV series) season 2|season two]] of ''[[The Masked Singer (American TV
